title: Event hub body redesign
question: Header stays. Which body language should Attendees, Listing, Forms, Images, and Settings share?

options.label: Continuous workbench
options.thesis: One calm stage under the header—no nested white cards. Dividers and density do the work.
options.viewport: Attendees: toolbar + segmented filters flush to the content plane; rows edge-to-edge; yellow only on Add.
options.risk: Can feel sparse if spacing is lazy.

options.label: Editorial twin + quiet ops
options.thesis: Listing feels like the public event page; ops tabs stay quieter and denser beside that twin.
options.viewport: Listing leads with large title and inline edit; Attendees/Forms/Images/Settings use the same quiet list grammar.
options.risk: Ops tabs can feel like a different product if the twin is too expressive.

options.label: Task planes
options.thesis: Each tab is one clear job surface with a strong primary action and ruthless hierarchy.
options.viewport: Every tab opens on the action that matters most that day; secondary controls recede until needed.
options.risk: Can feel pushy if every tab invents a hero CTA.
